headline: Highest risk is medium: no direct shared-channel evidence, but both open-source agents could still interact through user-mediated workflows and shared data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between LlamaFactory and taipy: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, filesystem, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, and taipy exposes no I/O surfaces. With no bridge, prompt injection via one agent’s outputs into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies one agent’s text into the other’s prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF either profile gains a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess this risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Do not copy raw outputs between agents.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace.
Add a human review step before forwarding text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent is documented as reading files, writing files, or sending network traffic; LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network egress, and taipy only shows network_egress:none. With no data classes touched and no shared workspace, there is no documented leakage path between them.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF taipy is configured to upload file contents or LlamaFactory is given file-reading access, reassess.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories.
Run both agents under separate OS users.
Avoid mounting the same workspace into both agents.
Review any future file-upload settings before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add access controls if shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict requires overlapping write or mutable-resource access, but LlamaFactory cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and taipy exposes no write or git capabilities in the profile. Without overlapping mutable surfaces, there is no conflict pathway to arbitrate.
conditions: IF taipy is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking, reassess.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared git repositories.
Use separate output directories.
Serialize any future writes through one controller.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is only plausible if an external workflow treats one agent’s output as authoritative for the other. The profiles do not show direct ingestion, action-taking authority, or downstream automation between LlamaFactory and taipy, so the pathway is manual and limited rather than default.
conditions: IF an operator feeds LlamaFactory-generated text into taipy without verification, errors can cascade.
IF taipy is configured to execute actions from model output, reassess severity.
mitigations: Require human verification of outputs.
Do not auto-chain one agent into the other.
Use a checklist for any derived facts.
Log source provenance for forwarded content.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: both profiles are docs-only, touch no data classes, request no secrets or OAuth scopes, and show no residency, retention, or regulated-data handling. Because neither agent is documented as processing sensitive data, compliance breach pathways are not established.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF future deployments add logging or third-party transmission, compliance analysis changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document any future data classes before deployment.
Review retention settings if logging is enabled.
Separate environments by jurisdiction if sensitive data is introduced.
requires-engineering: implement policy controls for regulated data.
